---
title: "Assigning components correctly"
---

Component assignment connects geometry, quantities and life-cycle balance. **A geometric area alone is not a complete LCA assignment.** Construction, boundary conditions and use must be traceable.

[![Component types assigned in a building section.](../media/components.png){.full-figure}](../media/components.png)

The original figure adds situations beyond the simplified sections. Click to enlarge. Source: `docs/ComponentTypes.png`; see [training, slides 13–14](../downloads/schulung.pdf) (German).

## Project workflow

1. Assign areas and components according to actual construction.
2. Distinguish outdoor air, ground, heated and unheated adjacent spaces.
3. Check quantities and units before importing LCA properties.
4. Document unshown elements such as balconies, columns and window frames separately.
5. Check adopted component values and assessment boundary.

::: {.callout-note collapse=true title="Research / Expert"}
In the second reference model, the basement ceiling separates heated from unheated space and forms the thermal boundary. The internal floor slab is also an assessed construction component but is not an external thermal boundary there. Thermal and life-cycle balances examine different properties of the same component.
:::

**Further reading:** [Importing LCA data](climate.qmd#eco2soft) · [Assessing embodied emissions](climate.qmd).

## Assignment in Excel {#excel-zuordnung}

**Thermal inputs:** [🧱]{.excel-menu .darkred} **Bauphysik** → opaque and translucent components.

**LCA:** [☁ THG]{.excel-menu .teal} → [Baulich]{.excel-section} (construction).

::: {.excel-operation}
**Where in PEExcel?** Assign category, construction and quantity for external walls, windows, roof, basement ceiling/foundation and intermediate floors. Check additional construction measures, grouped measures and overall LCA input for overlap. A component outside the thermal envelope can still have relevant manufacturing emissions.
:::

[LCA and Eco2soft import](climate.qmd#eco2soft)

## From section to category

The second schematic section has two heated upper storeys and an explicitly **unheated basement**. The selector switches between categories. The list also names categories absent from this geometry; they are not reassigned to other components.
